name: Poking Boop again and again keeps it angry
case: The person pokes Boop again and again, then again a minute later, and again a minute after that. Boop ends every round with an irritated or grumpy face (never a happy, excited or proud one), never swearing: a swear is for a failure, never at the person. Its mood climbs a step a round toward annoyed and irritated, as a mood moves a step at a time: engaged, curious or uneasy after the first, then on along the graph. By the end of the agent's next turn it is no further than irritated.
why: The one mood graph (2026-10-15): a mood moves one step along its pack's moves and holds at least 30 s (MoodPolicy), so a round of pokes moves the mood once, and grumpy is four steps from calm. PERSONALITY's Examples: pokes in a row get an annoyed, then irritated or grumpy face; characters/boop/steering/mood/: pokes in a row climb the mood graph to irritated and grumpy, more keep it there, and grumpy and irritated fade a step toward calm after their minutes, a single poke then being a fresh start. Every poke wakes the brain; each step checks its round's last, four in a row
